summary: A ROS Answers question from November 2022 by user GUENNI asks why a publisher declared with the C type name trajectory_msgs__msg__JointTrajectory fails to compile in ROS 2 Humble, producing a static assertion that the message type is not ROS-compatible. The answer by Mike Scheutzow advises using the C++ namespace form trajectory_msgs::msg::JointTrajectory, and a commenter, gvdhoorn, confirms the underscore form is the C type. The asker reports the fix removed most errors, leaving one remaining issue, and the page notes the site is deprecated in favor of Robotics Stack Exchange.
one_line: ROS 2 Humble C++ question on why a publisher for trajectory_msgs__msg__JointTrajectory fails, answered by using the C++ namespace form.
key_facts: The question was asked on 2022-11-07 by user GUENNI and tagged ros2, humble, C++, and JointTrajectory.

Compiling with rclcpp::Publisher<trajectory_msgs__msg__JointTrajectory>::SharedPtr produced a static assertion error that the given message type is not compatible with ROS and cannot be used with a Publisher.
The error originated in /opt/ros/humble/include/rclcpp/rclcpp/publisher.hpp at line 81, where rclcpp::is_ros_compatible_type<MessageT>::value is checked.
The asker reported that a standard string message type gave no error when used with a publisher.
Mike Scheutzow answered on 2022-11-07 that the ros2 minimal publisher example declares its publisher_ attribute using C++ namespace syntax.
Mike Scheutzow suggested using trajectory_msgs::msg::JointTrajectory instead of the underscore form.
gvdhoorn commented that trajectory_msgs__msg__JointTrajectory is indeed the C type.
The asker updated the question with corrected code using trajectory_msgs::msg::JointTrajectory and reported that most errors were gone with one error left.
The asker's node class HardwareCommandPub is named after the ToArduino_command_publisher node and publishes to the topic Joint_Value with queue size 10.
The hardware interface code sets joint_names for hip, shoulder, elbow, and wrist in on_init and writes command positions in write() before calling publishData.
The asker asked whether the two notations, the underscore form and the double-colon form, correspond to C and C++ respectively, and this was confirmed.
The ROS Answers site states it is deprecated as of August 11, 2023, and is read-only, with users directed to robotics.stackexchange.com.
